course.seoMetaDescription: Build, Ship & Scale Products Without Coding Fear
course.seoContent:
Build, Ship & Scale Products Without Coding Fear

Most founders today have ideas.

But they are stuck between two problems:

• Hiring developers without understanding technology

• Depending on expensive agencies to build products

• Or learning coding from scratch which takes years

This course solves that gap.

AI-Powered MVP Engineering for Non-Developers is designed to help founders, creators, and operators think like a technical founder — without becoming a traditional programmer.

Instead of teaching complicated coding theory, this program focuses on system thinking, product architecture, and AI-assisted development so that you can design, build, and launch real digital products.

By the end of this program, you will understand how modern products are built — from idea → architecture → development → deployment → scaling → launch.

You won’t just watch tutorials.

You will build working MVPs.

modules.title: MINDSET, VIBE CODING & PRODUCT THINKING
modules.description: This phase builds the foundational thinking required to build products with AI. Students learn how modern founders combine structured thinking with AI tools to rapidly create MVPs.

videoLessons.title: Introduction to Vibe Coding
videoLessons.description:
This chapter introduces the concept of vibe coding, a modern approach where founders use AI tools to translate product ideas into working software without deep programming expertise.
Students will learn how AI can act as a technical co-founder, assisting with writing code, debugging issues, and generating product components.
The chapter also explains the limitations of AI-driven development, including where AI struggles, why structure matters, and why founders still need strong product thinking.
By the end, students understand that AI development is not magic — it is structured thinking combined with intelligent tool usage.

videoLessons.title: Idea to MVP
videoLessons.description:
Most founders fail because they build too much before validating anything. This chapter teaches how to move from an idea to a functional MVP quickly.
Students will learn the real definition of an MVP and the difference between idea, prototype, MVP, product, and scalable system.
A simple framework is introduced to design products around problem → user → core action → value loop, helping founders focus on building only what truly matters.
By the end of this chapter, students will know how to prioritize features and avoid overbuilding.

videoLessons.title: Product-Market Fit & Pricing Models
videoLessons.description:
A product is only successful if it solves a problem people are willing to pay for.
In this chapter, students learn how to recognize product-market fit signals, detect when a product is failing, and adapt quickly.
The chapter also explains common monetization models used in modern digital products, including subscriptions, usage-based pricing, marketplace commissions, and freemium strategies.
Students will learn how to design early monetization strategies, so revenue begins before perfection.

videoLessons.title: PRD Basics
videoLessons.description:
A Product Requirement Document (PRD) is the blueprint of a digital product.
This chapter teaches founders how to structure product thinking into a clear technical document that developers or AI tools can follow.
Students will learn the essential sections of a PRD, including problem definition, target users, feature lists, product flows, edge cases, and success metrics.
By the end of this chapter, students will create their own MVP PRD, which will act as the foundation for building their product.

modules.title: CORE TECH FOUNDATIONS (NO JARGON BUT REAL)
modules.description: This phase explains how modern software systems actually work, using simple conceptual explanations rather than heavy programming theory.

videoLessons.title: Frontend vs Backend
videoLessons.description:
This chapter breaks down what actually happens when a user interacts with a digital product.
Students will learn the flow of modern applications:
User Interface → API → Business Logic → Database → Response.
Key architectural ideas such as client–server systems, modular design, and monolithic systems are explained in simple visual diagrams.
By the end of this chapter, students will clearly understand the technical anatomy of digital products.

videoLessons.title: UI/UX Basics
videoLessons.description:
Design is not decoration — it directly impacts revenue.
This chapter introduces the difference between User Interface (UI) and User Experience (UX) and explains why usability determines whether users stay or leave.
Students will learn the basics of wireframing, user journey design, and interface simplicity, along with an introduction to modern UI frameworks such as Tailwind and Bootstrap.
The focus is on creating simple, functional MVP designs rather than complex visual perfection.

videoLessons.title: Framework Selection
videoLessons.description:
Modern development involves choosing the right frameworks rather than building everything from scratch.
In this chapter, students learn what frameworks are and when to choose technologies like React, Next.js, Node.js, Django, or no-code tools.
A decision framework helps founders evaluate build vs buy decisions, ensuring they choose tools that match their product complexity and growth plans.
This helps founders avoid costly technical mistakes early in product development.

lessons.title: API Fundamentals, Database Basics, Authentication & Security

videoLessons.title: API Fundamentals, Database Basics, Authentication & Security
videoLessons.description:
APIs are the communication layer of modern software systems.
This chapter explains what APIs are and how different parts of a product communicate using requests and responses.
Students will learn the basic structure of REST APIs, including GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE operations, along with request structures, response formats, and status codes.
A mini project demonstrates how to create and test an API using AI assistance, helping students understand real backend communication. 
Every digital product stores and manages data.
This chapter introduces the role of databases and explains the difference between SQL and NoSQL systems.
Students will learn how data is structured using tables, relationships, and CRUD operations.
The chapter also covers basic data modeling techniques for MVP products, followed by a mini project where students set up a simple backend using tools like Postgres or Supabase.
User accounts are the backbone of most digital platforms.
This chapter explains how login systems work, including signup flows, password security, and authentication mechanisms.
Students will learn the conceptual difference between JWT tokens and session-based authentication, along with role-based access control for multi-user systems.
The chapter also highlights common security mistakes that cause many early-stage MVPs to get compromised.

course.mentorDescription:
Sahil Khanna, a seasoned Engineer turned Digital Marketing expert, stands as the visionary founder behind Intellectual Indies, a prominent digital marketing channel that has left an indelible mark on the industry, particularly in India. With a remarkable track record, Sahil has empowered over 1,40,000 entrepreneurs worldwide, translating his technical background into practical insights for the digital landscape.

For Sahil, the allure of money takes a backseat to the profound impact and positive difference he can instigate in someone’s life through his endeavors. His narrative is a testament to the transformative power of resilience, a testament to his commitment to making a meaningful impact in the world of business and marketing.

data.text: Traditional programming courses teach you how to become a developer.
This program teaches you how to become a technical founder.
Instead of spending years learning every programming detail, you will learn how products are designed, built, deployed and scaled in the real world.
The goal is not to turn you into a full-time programmer.
The goal is to help you build, launch and manage technology products intelligently using AI-assisted development.

data.text: This program is designed to transform you from someone who only has product ideas into someone who can design, build, deploy, and launch real digital products.
Instead of spending years learning traditional programming, you will learn how modern products actually work and how to use AI-assisted development to build MVPs faster.
By the end of this program, you will have a clear understanding of product architecture, system flows, and deployment processes, along with the confidence to launch your own tech products.
You will also build multiple real MVP projects, helping you understand the entire lifecycle of product development — from idea to launch.
This course focuses on practical execution so that you leave not just with knowledge, but with working products and a technical founder mindset.

frameworkSection.title: The 6-Phase Founder Tech Framework
frameworkSection.subtitle: A structured roadmap to go from idea → MVP → scalable product

data.text: Most courses either teach coding theory or random tools without explaining how real products are built.
This program follows a structured 6-phase framework used by modern product teams and technical founders.
Instead of jumping directly into coding, you will first understand how products are designed, architected, and validated, and then move into building real systems.
The goal is simple:Help you move from idea-stage founder → product-building founder.
Phase 1 — Product Thinking & Vibe Coding Mindset

Understand how modern founders use AI as a technical co-founder.You will learn product thinking, MVP definition, feature prioritization, pricing models, and how to write clear Product Requirement Documents (PRDs).
Phase 2 — Core Tech Foundations
Learn how digital products actually work.You will understand frontend vs backend, APIs, databases, authentication systems, UI/UX basics, and framework selection for MVPs.
Phase 3 — Servers, Cloud & Deployment
Discover how applications go live on the internet.You will learn servers, hosting, domains, DNS, environment variables, cloud platforms, and the basics of DevOps and deployment pipelines.
Phase 4 — Building Real MVP Products
This is where theory turns into practice.You will build multiple real MVP systems including a SaaS dashboard, marketplace platform, and an AI-powered product.
Phase 5 — Testing & Scaling

Understand what happens when your product starts growing.You will learn debugging mindset, error handling, testing basics, logging, scaling challenges, caching concepts, and infrastructure cost management.
Phase 6 — Launch & Product Growth
Learn how to launch products and turn MVPs into real businesses.You will explore beta testing, feedback loops, product iterations, AI-powered marketing systems, and startup metrics like CAC and LTV.

data.text: Many founders and creators have powerful product ideas but get stuck at one critical stage — building the product.
The biggest problem is not the idea.The problem is technical execution.
Most people fall into one of these situations:
They depend completely on developers, spend huge amounts on agencies, or try to learn programming from scratch and get overwhelmed.
At the same time, AI tools are evolving rapidly, but without the right understanding of product architecture, system flows, and deployment, most people cannot use them effectively.
This course solves that gap.
Instead of teaching complicated programming theory, this program helps you understand how modern digital products actually work and how to use AI tools to build MVPs intelligently.
You will learn how to go from idea → MVP → product launch with a structured system used by modern technical founders.
